name: What kitchen size is actually allowed in a Los Angeles ADU without wasting square footage?

mainEntity.name: How small can an ADU kitchen be in Los Angeles and still qualify as a full kitchen?
mainEntity.text: How small can an ADU kitchen be in Los Angeles and still qualify as a full kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: A well-designed ADU kitchen in Los Angeles should be compact, but it still needs to function like a real kitchen. The key is not just square footage; it is whether the layout supports required appliances, prep space, storage, and safe circulation. In many ADUs, a single-wall or galley layout works better than forcing an island into a small footprint. The best approach is to prioritize the sink, cooking surface, refrigerator, landing space, and enough counter area to cook comfortably without crowding the room. Poorly planned layouts often feel bigger on paper but perform worse in daily use. A good designer or contractor will also account for door swings, appliance clearances, utility runs, and whether the kitchen should visually open into the living area. For homeowners in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, the best kitchen size is usually the smallest layout that still feels complete, code-aware, and easy to maintain.
acceptedAnswer.description: A Los Angeles ADU kitchen must include a sink, cooking appliance, food prep space, storage, and a refrigerator to count as a full kitchen. The ideal size depends on layout efficiency, but even compact ADU kitchens should preserve clear work zones, appliance clearance, and code-compliant circulation rather than trying to maximize cabinet count.
